Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

a man of phrase

describing someone or something by a quality: of great courage, of few words, of small build

also of great courage, a man of few words, a woman of great kindness, of small build, of that kind, a boy of three, a three-year-old boy, with blue eyes

classical

Cic. Fam. 9.26.3: nōn multī cibī hospitem accipiēs, multī jocī

vir magnī animī

the genitive of quality: a noun in the genitive with an adjective, describing another noun

a man of great spirit

English “of” with a quality is a genitive in Latin, but only when the quality has an adjective: vir magnī animī, never vir animī (Allen & Greenough §345). It is the regular form for measure, number and age: puer trium annōrum, a boy of three; fossa trium pedum, a three-foot ditch.

Other words

  • vir magnō animō — a man of great spirit

    the ablative of quality: a noun in the ablative with an adjective · also used · classical · Gell. 19.13.2–3: parvā nimis statūrā hominēs; brevī atque humilī corpore hominēs

    The ablative does the same work and is the usual case for the body and its looks: parvā statūrā, of small build; caeruleīs oculīs, with blue eyes (Allen & Greenough §415).

  • ejus modī — of that kind

    also used · classical

    A genitive of quality that has become a fixed phrase (see kind).

Examples

  • nōn multī cibī hospitem accipiēs, multī jocī

    you’ll be entertaining a guest of small appetite and plenty of jokesCic. Fam. 9.26.3

  • nānōs dīcere parvā nimis statūrā hominēs

    to call people of very small build “nānī”Gell. 19.13.2

See also age, kind, what kind of, three years old, quality.

SourcesThe examples are from the Latīnitās loci collections and the note on quantity words, checked there against the texts. The rule is Allen & Greenough’s (§§345, 415).
